title: POC scoping: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private - Monarch Biotech
customer_attendees: Dr. Lina Patel, Head of ML
summary: Initial POC scoping to decide between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment. Discussed success criteria (latency, throughput, data residency), workload size, benchmarks to run, rough timeline (4-6 weeks), and next steps: share pricing, security docs, run benchmark with sample dataset, and schedule follow-up SE-led benchmark session.
topics: Success criteria: latency SLOs, accuracy, cost per token
Workload sizing: QPS, average request length, peak concurrency
Benchmarks: perf tests, regression checks, embedding quality
Deployment tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Security/compliance: SOC 2, KMS, audit logs, data residency
Timeline and next steps for POC
transcription_text:
Meeting header: 2026-03-17 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes | Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Lina Patel, Rajiv Menon, Sofia Alvarez, Ethan Cole

[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intro - I'm Ava, AE at Redwood, and Mateo's our solutions engineer.
[00:06] Dr. Lina Patel: Hi, Lina here. Thanks. We're trying to scope a POC for Monarch's internal assistant and some document search embedding workloads.
[00:12] Rajiv Menon: Hey all, Rajiv. Main goals are low latencies for chat, and embeddings for search with decent cost envelopes.
[00:18] Mateo Ruiz: Great. Can I...can I start with a couple of clarifying questions about traffic and success criteria?
[00:22] Dr. Lina Patel: Sure. We're expecting baseline 5 qps across production, peaking to about 40 qps during shift start. Most requests are short, 50-150 tokens, but some long gen flows up to 1k tokens for summarization. Embedding workload is batched roughly 200-500 docs hourly.
[00:38] Ava Chen: Good, so qps + burst profile captured. What's your latency target for chat?
[00:42] Rajiv Menon: 200-300 ms p95 for short turn completions would be ideal; for longer summaries we can tolerate up to 1s.
[00:49] Sofia Alvarez: And note - data residency: PHI-ish data, so we'd prefer private or VPC options, but would consider Dedicated if we get a strong contractual guarantee and KMS/HSM integration.
[00:58] Mateo Ruiz: Okay makes sense. So the three flavors: Hosted gives fastest time to value and managed infra, Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation, Private gives customer-managed control and on-prem options for highest compliance.
[01:12] Dr. Lina Patel: Right, and cost is also a factor. We want an estimate of cost per 1k tokens and cost for embedding throughput so we can compare.
[01:20] Ava Chen: We'll share pricing ranges; for the POC we typically recommend a 4-6 week pilot where we validate latency and accuracy and run perf benchmarks against your real workloads.
[01:28] Ethan Cole: We also need audit logs, SSO with SAML, RBAC, and ability to push policies to logs for retention 7 years-ish.
[01:36] Mateo Ruiz: Redwood supports SAML SSO and RBAC. Audit logs / long tail retention are available as an add-on; for Private deployment you get customer-managed logging. We'll put links in follow-up.
[01:44] Dr. Lina Patel: Ok can you give us what you'd run as benchmarks?
[01:47] Mateo Ruiz: Sure. We'd do three buckets: 1) Synthetic latency tests across short/long sequences to validate p95 targets; 2) Throughput stress tests with concurrency to observe scaling and tail latency; 3) Quality/regression checks on a sample of your prompts to ensure model fidelity and hallucination rates. For embeddings, we'd run batch ingestion and run similarity queries to measure embedding latency and recall against your gold-set.
[02:09] Rajiv Menon: For embeddings, recall at 10 (R@10) and latency for top-k lookup are important.
[02:13] Ava Chen: Noted. Any constraints on providing sample data for the perf runs? We can obfuscate or you can run tests on-prem if needed.
[02:19] Sofia Alvarez: We'll probably provide a de-identified sample dataset first. For the final security review we may require on-prem tests or a Private deployment.
[02:26] Mateo Ruiz: That matches many customers. For POC mechanics: if you want Hosted POC, we run tests in Redwood's hosted env with your sample data; Dedicated POC means we spin up reserved nodes for the duration; Private is longer lead time - usually need network setup, VPN/VPC peering and can add 2-4 weeks of ops work.
[02:44] Dr. Lina Patel: Lead time for Private is a blocker for our 6-week launch window.
[02:48] Rajiv Menon: Right - can we do a hybrid? Start with Hosted for benchmarks and then move to Dedicated or Private for production?
[02:55] Ava Chen: Yes, that's a common path. Redwood supports canary rollouts and model pinning, so you can prototype on Hosted then transition to Dedicated with the same API.
[03:03] Ethan Cole: We'll need to understand encryption: in transit and at rest, and KMS integration for Dedicated and Private.
[03:09] Mateo Ruiz: We support TLS everywhere. For at-rest encryption we integrate with customer KMS on Dedicated and Private; Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default but we can do customer KMS via contractual options for higher tiers.
[03:19] Dr. Lina Patel: What about quantization or model variants? We care about quality loss; we don't want to drop below current baseline for summarization.
[03:26] Mateo Ruiz: For POC we can test both FP16/FP32 and quantized variants. Our Optimize tooling can recommend quant profiles per workload; we'll measure ROUGE/BLEU or your preferred metrics to show any degradation.
[03:36] Rajiv Menon: Can you run example costs? Say for 100M tokens/month + embeddings for 1M docs ingestion per month.
[03:44] Ava Chen: We'll provide an estimate in the pricing sheet. Ballpark: hosted is easiest but unit cost tends to be higher than dedicated. Dedicated amortizes over reserved capacity and can reduce cost by 20-40% depending on utilization. Private has higher fixed setup but can be best for compliance and sometimes cost if you have infra already. We'll send numbers.
[04:03] Dr. Lina Patel: Great. For success criteria: we'll define final success as: p95 latency < 300 ms for short chat flows, throughput to handle 40 qps with acceptable tail, R@10 > current baseline for embeddings, and cost per 1k tokens under a target TBD.
[04:17] Sofia Alvarez: Plus security signoff: SOC 2 / ISO docs, KMS, SSO, and audit capabilities.
[04:23] Mateo Ruiz: Sounds good. On benchmarks, we suggest running the latency and throughput suite first, and concurrently run embedding recall tests. We'll produce a benchmark script and a results dashboard link.
[04:34] Rajiv Menon: Timeline - can we do initial hosted benchmarks in 1 week once we share data?
[04:38] Ava Chen: Yes, 1 week for hosted perf/run if samples are available; 2-4 weeks if we need deeper regression checks. Dedicated pilot provisioning takes ~1 week to schedule, Private provisioning 3-6 weeks depending on networking.
[04:50] Ethan Cole: Ok that helps. About logs and retention - can you send the retention options and pricing?
[04:54] Ava Chen: Yes. We'll include it in the security/pricing pack.
[04:58] Dr. Lina Patel: Any notable competitors / comparisons you think we should be aware of?
[05:02] Mateo Ruiz: Customers often evaluate against Anthropic, OpenAI, and self-hosted runtimes like KServe/Anyscale or LangServe variants. We'll call out differences in performance and operational overhead.
[05:14] Rajiv Menon: Also looking at GCP Vertex for long term for embeddings.
[05:18] Ava Chen: We'll include a short competitive matrix.
[05:21] Dr. Lina Patel: Ok let's recap next steps.
[05:23] Ava Chen: Recap: 1) Redwood to share POC pricing ranges and dedicated vs hosted cost comparison; 2) Redwood to share SOC 2/ISO docs, KMS integration notes, audit/logging options; 3) Customer to provide de-identified sample dataset and a small gold-set for embedding recall; 4) Schedule a 90-minute SE-led benchmark run - target next Wednesday 2026-03-25 14:00 UTC (tentative).
[05:46] Sofia Alvarez: And we'll review the security pack with our compliance team.
[05:49] Rajiv Menon: Do you have any checklist for network setup if we go Private?
[05:53] Mateo Ruiz: Yes - VPC peering, firewall rules, IP whitelisting, bastion host details. We'll attach the checklist.
[05:59] Ava Chen: Great. Any other questions?
[06:01] Dr. Lina Patel: No, that covers it. Thanks everyone.
[06:04] Ava Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule. Bye.

Notes: Transcription contains minor mis-hearings typical of automated transcripts (e.g., KMS sometimes transcribed as 'K M S' and 'Anyscale' as 'any scale').
